description: We are a passionate team from Bhaktapur, Nepal, excited to build innovative solutions for space exploration. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we are working on astronaut health monitoring software, combining software development, cybersecurity, AI/ML, data analysis, and design. We welcome creative and motivated members with skills in healthcare, space science, AI/ML, UI/UX, research, and storytelling.
summary:
AstroVitals is a mission-health monitoring prototype built by Team Vital Orbit. It gives astronauts a live dashboard showing heart rate, SpO2, blood pressure, temperature, respiration and HRV, along with a readiness score, daily wellness check-ins and lifetime trends. When a reading turns critical (cardiac hypoxia, severe bradycardia or low oxygen), the app shows an emergency banner with precautions and speaks the warning aloud for hands-free guidance until the astronaut acknowledges it.
Ground Control gets a separate secure portal to review each astronaut's telemetry, alert history and check-ins, and to send warnings or suggestions that arrive in real time through a delayed-link inbox.
The frontend uses React and Vite. Supabase handles the database, authentication, realtime updates and security rules. An optional FastAPI service adds anomaly detection and risk scoring. AstroVitals is a demonstration tool using simulated data, not a medical device, and it would need clinical and safety validation before any real use.
details:
Project: AstroVitals, an astronaut mission-health monitoring and Ground Control decision-support tool

Team: Vital Orbit

Status: Implemented prototype (demonstration data only, not a medical device)

Users

Astronaut: picks one of three seeded profiles (MAGNUM / Astronaut Jenny, HELLBORNE / Ross Strider, BREEZE / Reed Mutt), sets a password of at least 8 characters, and sees only their own data.

Ground Control operator: signs in with Supabase Auth at /ground-control.

Key features

Live telemetry every 5 seconds: heart rate, SpO2, blood pressure, temperature, respiration, HRV. Every fourth sample is saved to Supabase.

Nominal, watch and critical states, plus a readiness score.

Critical rules: cardiac hypoxia (HR > 135 and SpO2 < 94%), severe bradycardia (HR < 45), critical oxygen (SpO2 < 92%).

Emergency banner, precautions and repeating voice warning until the astronaut acknowledges.

One daily check-in per UTC day: sleep, mood, stress, fatigue, pain, appetite, exercise, resistance and notes.

Lifetime trends for each metric.

Ground Control can switch astronauts, review telemetry, alerts and check-ins, and send warnings or suggestions. Messages arrive in real time and can be read aloud.

Tech stack

Frontend: React 19, Vite 8, plain CSS, browser Speech Synthesis.

Backend and data: Supabase (Postgres, Auth, RPCs, Realtime, Row Level Security).

Optional analysis service: FastAPI with a nearest-centroid model. Endpoints are /health, /predict, /baseline, /anomaly, /risk and /messages.

Hosting: Vercel for the frontend, a separate Python host for the API.

Database Tables: astronauts, vitals, checkins, alerts, astronaut_credentials, ground_control_messages

Roadmap: real wearable data, identity-based Ground Control roles, connecting the analysis service to the dashboard, offline queueing, and clinical and safety validation before any real use.
